title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
authors: Ao Chen, Johnnie Gray, Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.
summary: This paper investigates the complex ground state of the hole-doped Hubbard model, which is crucial for understanding high-temperature superconductivity. By employing advanced neural tensor network simulations, the authors demonstrate that the system does not favor a single ordered state but rather exists in a regime of extreme competition between superconducting pairing and charge/spin stripe formation. This work significantly advances the numerical understanding of strongly correlated electron physics.
main_problem: To resolve the uncertainty regarding the ground state order (superconductivity vs. stripes) in the hole-doped Hubbard model, which is highly sensitive to computational methods.
main_result: The work suggests a picture of extreme competition between stripe order and superconductivity, revealing a near degeneracy among several competing low-energy states at 1/8 doping.
method: The authors employed state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, achieving high variational accuracy on large lattices.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the two-dimensional Hubbard model, a minimal model for cuprate high-temperature superconductors, analyzed at $1/8$ hole doping and including next-nearest-neighbor hopping.
key_observables: d-wave pairing order parameter ($\Delta_{2SC}$), stripe order parameter ($M_{2str}$), and energy per site ($E/N$).
important_parameters: Hole doping of $1/8$, next-nearest-neighbor hopping ($t'$), and the Hubbard interaction ($U$).
main_assumptions: The authors extrapolate results to the thermodynamic limit using linear or quadratic fits, and the use of backflow states is noted to bias the state toward superconductivity.
figures_summary: Figures compare the energies and order parameters ($\Delta_{2SC}$ vs $M_{2str}$) for different candidate states (stripe, SC, mixed) at various doping levels and hopping parameters.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares results from multiple variational wavefunctions (BCS, Pfaffian, NN-fPEPS) by calculating key order parameters and extrapolating energies to estimate the true ground state, culminating in a discussion of the competition between orders.
why_interesting: The advanced use of neural tensor networks (NN-fPEPS) to tackle strongly correlated electron models represents a cutting-edge application of machine learning to condensed matter physics, providing highly accurate benchmarks for complex quantum systems.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
